title: Two-round ordinary-source refinement to the Dirichlet boundary 0.874771265
description:
We prove that, for every positive modulus and every complex Dirichlet character χ, the Dirichlet L-function L(s,χ) is nonzero whenever Re(s) > 174954253/200000000 = 0.874771265, excluding the principal pole at χ = 1 and s = 1. This is a parameter refinement of existing machinery, not a new analytic method.

The proof starts from the full Hecke-family bound 8747729897/10000000000 formalized in Hailey Collet's sources, which the admitted Lewko submission vendors, and applies two ordered, acyclic ordinary-source returns: round A reaches 87477127/100000000 and round B reaches 174954253/200000000. Each round lowers the natural root price to 6(2θ_input − 1), keeps the NF rule's fixed internal reference 11243277/2500000, rebuilds the finite source graph and certifies a common-envelope physical return. Each graph has 21,527 count and 19,529 physical transitions; every child uses its predecessor as both its LOW and HIGH supplier, with allowance and fees 10^-17, 10^-12 and 10^-10. Each return uses 38 non-old admission windows, each checking all fifteen admissibility guards, 224 exact Bernstein row boxes and reserve 10^-9. The inverse input is the original unconditional estimate with price 2. Conjecture C and any improved inverse-moment hypothesis are neither proved nor assumed. All rational witnesses and certificates are in the Lean source.

Round A follows the adaptive-cap construction first proposed, as an exact-rational computation without Lean verification, in rohanarun/quasi-rh-hillclimb PR #28. Research, exact computation, Lean development and drafting were substantially AI-assisted with OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude. We credit Hailey Collet for the ordinary-source construction, NF theorem and finite Bernstein return; Mark Lewko for the admitted coherent development and generic transport and schedule interfaces; and OpenAI for the analytic framework. The transitive development retains contributions by Akash Levy, Zhongpai Gao, timbalud, DaysSky, liqsweep and ArviFoxy, with their upstream notices. Lean, mathlib, the PrimeNumberTheoremAnd package by Alex Kontorovich and contributors, and Adam Benenson's Rellich–Kondrachov package retain their original authorship, licenses and notices.
